nodes.summary: There is a finitely generated hereditarily just infinite group $G$ such that for no field $K$ and no natural number $n$ is there an injective group homomorphism $G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$.
nodes.title: Not every finitely generated hereditarily just infinite group is linear

nodes.summary: The proposition that every finitely generated hereditarily just infinite group $G$ is linear, i.e. that there are a field $K$, a natural number $n$ and an injective group homomorphism $G \to \mathrm{GL}_n(K)$.
nodes.title: Kourovka 15.18(b): linearity of hereditarily just infinite groups

nodes.summary: There is a finitely generated hereditarily just infinite group $G$ in which every element has finite order.
nodes.title: Finitely generated hereditarily just infinite torsion groups exist

nodes.summary: The proposition that there exists a finitely generated hereditarily just infinite group $G$ that is a torsion group, i.e. every element of $G$ has finite order.
nodes.title: Kourovka 15.18(a): hereditarily just infinite torsion groups

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a generating family of a group $G$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, and let $\beta_P(n)$ be the number of elements of $G$ whose word length with respect to $P$ is at most $n$, that is, which are products of at most $n$ members of $P$ and their inverses. The growth rate of $P$ is the real number $\omega(G, P) = \limsup_{n \to \infty} \beta_P(n)^{1/n}$.
nodes.title: Growth rate of a finite generating family

nodes.summary: A group $G$ has intermediate growth if it is finitely generated and, for every natural number $k$ and every generating family $P$ of $G$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, k-1\}$, the growth rate of $P$ is at most $1$ (subexponential growth) and $P$ does not have polynomial growth.
nodes.title: Groups of intermediate growth

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is a branch group (Kourovka 15.12) if there are a sequence $m : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ with $m(i) \ge 2$ for all $i$ and a homomorphism $\rho$ from $G$ to the group of permutations of the vertices of the rooted tree with branching sequence $m$ such that $\rho$ is injective; every $\rho(g)$ is a tree automorphism, that is, for all vertices $v$ and $w$, $v$ is a prefix of $w$ if and only if…
nodes.title: Branch groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is hereditarily just infinite (in the sense of Kourovka 15.18) if it is infinite, residually finite, and every nontrivial normal subgroup of $G$, viewed as a group in its own right, is just infinite.
nodes.title: Hereditarily just infinite groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is just infinite if it is infinite and every nontrivial normal subgroup of $G$ has finite index, that is, all proper quotients of $G$ are finite.
nodes.title: Just infinite groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is just infinite if it is infinite and every nontrivial normal subgroup of $G$ has finite index in $G$.
nodes.title: Just infinite groups

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is residually finite if every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ lies outside some normal subgroup of finite index in $G$.
nodes.title: Residually finite groups

nodes.summary: It is not the case that every finitely generated just infinite group of intermediate growth is a branch group: the Kourovka Archive answers Problem 15.17 "No, not every".
nodes.title: Just infinite groups of intermediate growth need not be branch groups

nodes.summary: Kourovka Problem 15.17 (L. Bartholdi, R. I. Grigorchuk, Z. Šunić) is the assertion that every finitely generated just infinite group of intermediate growth is a branch group.
nodes.title: The branch question for just infinite groups of intermediate growth

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a homomorphism from a group $G$ to the group of permutations of the vertices of the rooted tree with branching sequence $m$. For a natural number $n$, the $n$-th rigid level stabilizer is the subgroup of $G$ generated by the union of the rigid vertex stabilizers of all vertices at level $n$, that is, of all words of length $n$.
nodes.title: Rigid level stabilizer

nodes.summary: Let $\rho$ be a homomorphism from a group $G$ to the group of permutations of the vertices of the rooted tree with branching sequence $m$, and let $v$ be a vertex. The rigid vertex stabilizer of $v$ is the set of elements $g \in G$ such that $\rho(g)$ fixes every vertex that does not have $v$ as a prefix, that is, the elements whose support (the set of vertices they move) lies in the subtree rooted at $v$.
nodes.title: Rigid vertex stabilizer

nodes.summary: For a sequence $m : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ of branching indices, the vertices of the spherically homogeneous rooted tree with branching sequence $m$ are the finite words $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{\ell-1}$ of natural numbers with $x_i < m(i)$ for every $i < \ell$. The length of a word is its level and its prefixes are its ancestors.
nodes.title: Vertices of a spherically homogeneous rooted tree

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
